$comment: Shared project settings for every Claude Code session in this repository (incident-platform backlog #0-269, AC5). The denies are incident-platform's .claude/settings.json's that apply here, kept in the same order; dispatcher/test/session-denies.test.mjs fails when one is missing (the drift between the two lists is incident-platform #0-268's). Why they exist: a session the owner starts in this repository's clone on the host runs gh with the owner's own login, an admin's, which the rulesets of main and of tags do not bind; so it may not merge with the bypass (--admin, or the merge API), change a ruleset, a setting (a PATCH of the repository, gh repo edit), a collaborator, an environment or a secret, give the code owner's approval (gh pr review, the reviews API), push a tag (--tags, --follow-tags, --mirror and every abbreviation git accepts, a refs/tags/ refspec, `git push <remote> tag <t>`), write a release, or create, move or delete a git ref through the API. Inside the factory's devcontainer the session holds the token of the app profitbuild-factory-dev instead, and GitHub itself refuses it a push to main, a merge of a pull request the owner has not approved, a review that counts, a tag, a change to .github/workflows/, and every ruleset, setting, collaborator, environment and secret (ADR-0060 D5 as amended): for those the denies are a second line. They are the only line there for a release on a tag that exists and for a branch ref created or deleted through the API, which Contents write allows the app; and nothing here stops the deletion of a branch other than main by a push (`git push origin --delete <b>`, `git push origin :<b>`), which only the code owner's review of what was lost would notice (main and the tags are the rulesets'). Deny rules match the text of a command: they do not see `git -C <dir> push`, `bash -c`, a tag pushed by its bare name, or a push whose configuration (push.followTags, remote.<r>.mirror, remote.<r>.push) sends tags. They stop a mistake, not a command shaped to get past them. Changes need the owner's review (CODEOWNERS).
